methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses one cancer cell line (AGS) and one normal gastric epithelial line (HGEpiCs) with a panel of established assays (ATP viability, H2DCF-DA ROS, GSH-Glo, DiOC6 MMP, AO/EB apoptosis, alkaline comet) to characterize TQ-ox activity. At least four independent biological replicates are stated, with Shapiro-Wilk normality testing and ANOVA with Tukey post hoc. However, the selectivity window between AGS and HGEpiCs is narrow (IC50 40.29 vs 46.42 uM, ~15%), undermining claims of tumor-selective cytotoxicity. No molecular apoptosis markers (caspase cleavage, Annexin V) are included beyond AO/EB morphology, and the HGEpiC comparator shows similar ROS/GSH/MMP/comet responses, which limits mechanistic specificity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an in vitro preclinical study with a single gastric cancer cell line and no in vivo validation (Oxford LoE 5). The authors themselves acknowledge the need for in vivo validation and additional GC subtypes. Translational relevance is speculative given the narrow cancer vs normal selectivity and absence of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic data.

reporting_quality.justification: No formal preclinical reporting standard (ARRIVE does not apply to in vitro studies) is invoked, so 'other' is selected. Methods are detailed with reagent catalog numbers, fluorescence wavelengths, incubation conditions, and cell densities. However, there is no data/code availability statement, no raw blot or flow figures in main text, and key statistical details (exact n per experiment beyond 'at least four', exact P values beyond thresholds) are limited. The synthesis of TQ-ox references a prior publication rather than reproducing characterization.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors' own prior work has already established TQ-ox cytotoxicity, ROS induction, GSH depletion, MMP loss, and DNA damage in melanoma (Bozali et al. 2025, ref 17), HepG2 liver cancer (Guler & Bozali 2024, ref 11), SKOV-3 ovarian cancer (Kale et al. 2023, ref 8), and A549 lung cancer (Beyaztas et al. 2024, ref 27). This manuscript extends the same experimental battery to AGS gastric cells. The paper is therefore a direct, incremental replication of the authors' prior series in a new cell line rather than a novel mechanistic or chemical advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally clear with standard IMRaD organization and methodical description of each assay. The Discussion effectively contextualizes findings against the authors' prior TQ-ox work. Some redundancy across Results and Discussion, and the Introduction's oxime-chemistry paragraph is tangential. Supplementary figures are referenced for AO/EB and comet images, which is appropriate.

key_strengths: Integrated characterization across cytotoxicity, redox (ROS/GSH), mitochondrial (MMP), genotoxic (comet), and apoptotic (AO/EB) endpoints in a single cell-line pair
Inclusion of a normal HGEpiC comparator allowing preliminary selectivity assessment
Detailed methodology with reagent sourcing and four independent biological replicates
key_concerns: Narrow selectivity index (IC50 40 vs 46 uM) undermines claims of tumor-preferential activity
No in vivo validation and only one gastric cancer cell line tested (acknowledged limitation)
Highly incremental relative to the authors' own prior TQ-ox work in melanoma, liver, ovarian, and lung cancer cell lines
No molecular apoptosis markers (caspase cleavage, Annexin V/PI flow) beyond morphological AO/EB staining
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent but incremental preclinical in vitro study replicating the authors' prior TQ-ox findings in a new cell line, with limited selectivity window. Suitable for a lower-tier specialty journal with minor revisions.
